title: Point htmx verb attributes at same-origin paths, never absolute URLs

facts.note: Detector scan scope: templates and script/component source that can emit htmx markup.

values: htmx_hypermedia_detector: verb attribute value begins http://, https:// or //
facts.note: The detector scans the whole template/source set (not only the diff); its findings, including on unchanged existing attributes, must be surfaced to activation.

fires: A template or component contains an element with hx-get="https://api.example.com/orders", whether newly added or already present and unchanged.
A verb attribute (hx-post/hx-put/hx-patch/hx-delete) carries a protocol-relative value such as //host/path.
A verb attribute points at a staging or third-party host.
doesNotFire: A verb attribute carries a path-only value (/orders, ./orders, orders).
Only non-verb htmx attributes are involved (hx-target, hx-swap, hx-trigger).
Server-side handler code calls a remote upstream from behind a same-origin route.

given: A scanned template or source file contains an htmx verb attribute (hx-get, hx-post, hx-put, hx-patch, hx-delete — attributes that make an element issue an HTTP request).
when: The agent works in that code; every verb attribute present is in scope, including existing unchanged ones.
then: Every verb attribute MUST address a same-origin path (root-relative, e.g. /api/orders, resolved against the document's origin) and MUST NOT carry an absolute (http://, https://) or protocol-relative (//host/…) URL.
prefer: Replace the absolute URL with the path: hx-get="/api/orders", not hx-get="https://api.example.com/orders".
If the upstream is genuinely remote, add a same-origin proxy route on the server (e.g. /api/orders via Bun.serve) whose handler calls upstream, so the origin decision lives in one auditable place.
Use the same-origin path form for every hypermedia control in the app.
avoid: Baking a foreign, staging or third-party host into a verb attribute.
Scattering cross-origin decisions across templates instead of a server proxy route.
Suppressing an absolute-URL endpoint finding — it is not suppressible.
unless: Path-only values (/orders, ./orders, orders) are same-origin and never flagged.
Non-verb htmx attributes (hx-target, hx-swap, hx-trigger) are out of scope: they carry selectors and modifiers, not endpoints.
why: htmx swaps the response markup straight into the live DOM with no parse step, so the endpoint origin is a trust boundary: a foreign origin fails three ways — CORS breaks once it drops permissive headers, it is an untrusted-HTML injection point, and a baked-in staging host reaches production invisible to env vars and config review.
evidence: htmx_hypermedia_detector reports no verb attribute whose value begins http://, https:// or // anywhere in the scanned templates and source (existing and new).
Any genuinely required cross-origin call is reachable only via a same-origin server route whose handler performs the upstream call.
verifier_detail: Detector: zero-dependency Bun detector (htmx_hypermedia_detector family on atdd.workspace.bun) scanning .html/.htm templates and .ts/.tsx/.js/.jsx/.mjs source.
Flag a verb attribute (hx-get, hx-post, hx-put, hx-patch, hx-delete) whose value begins http://, https:// or //.
Never flag path-only values (/orders, ./orders, orders); ignore non-verb hx-* attributes (hx-target, hx-swap, hx-trigger).
Disposition strict, severity 2: an absolute-URL endpoint finding is not suppressible.
audit: schema_version 1.1.0; kind rule; status active; introduced_in 0.1.0.
Bun/htmx-stack realization of the agnostic "a client must not hardcode a foreign origin" obligation; enforced by the htmx_hypermedia_detector family implementation on atdd.workspace.bun.
Summary: an "htmx endpoints are same-origin paths" obligation.
